classification: Three reviewed actual-sign template and Boolean-attainability theorems; original convergence OPEN
conclusions: Sparse independent flips of regular Hadamard matrices realize a flat singular bulk and finitely many template outliers in actual complete cross sign matrices.
Under q=||C||op>=1 and tau(C)=p q, the realized matrices have normalized SDP value tending to q and asymptotically optimal scalar duals; exact finite-order scalar optimality is not asserted.
The completion Gamma is an upper certificate. For finite scalar-optimal templates tau(C)=p q, matched-frame clipping gives Gamma>283/200>sqrt(2) when q>=5/2.
A modified Hadamard background fixes a full Boolean algebra with independently dense exact block-mean grids. It yields the genuine actual lower Lambda_I.
For symmetric PSD templates, Lambda_I=Gamma and the actual normalized Boolean norm tends to this common value.
A symmetric positive quadratic top frame gives an actual lower 1+D_f(q); unit clipping yields actual liminf>1.524049912 for q>=5/2. Dilation supplies such a frame but changes the large sign family.
not_proved: A low-Boolean-norm nonsymmetric template at the problematic parameters.
Exact scalar optimality of a finite realized signing.
Equality of Gamma with actual Boolean norm for general nonsymmetric templates.
The general conditional Gaussian leading comparison, original all-orders convergence, or an identified limit value.
next_target: Use actual coordinate/optimal-frame and source compatibility to address the remaining nonsymmetric low-norm case or the general Gaussian upper; do not substitute a Gamma upper-certificate obstruction for an actual Boolean lower.
